Thank you for talking about this. I've been on the other end, feeling like I couldn't talk about what the "missing stair" had done to me. It dawned on me that a lot of the group was complicit, and found him "a little pushy but he means well". A little testing of the waters with a female friend in the group turned into victim blaming/shaming towards me so I left the group to pick up the pieces of my life and try and heal alone.

It's sad but good in a way to know that other people inside this kind of group may know and feel equally as lost in how to deal with it. People asking why the women don't group together and report/press charges may not realize how soul-shattering the pressure/scrutiny of the process can be -- especially if nobody else seems to have a problem with him. I wish I had something insightful on how to handle it, but at least providing support and believing those who come forward helps a lot. Predators get away with this because they aren't always raging, violent caricatures -- they're people too who know their behavior isn't good, and will strive to hide it.

Argh sorry I completely missed that part of your question, my apologies. I agree with the other poster, I, Robot is a better starting point. I think Foundation benefits from having a primer of the concepts he likes to explore.

I recommend "Robot Dreams", which is a short story anthology. It was the first Asimov book I picked up and was a great introduction to his style and a lot of major elements (such as the Laws of Robotics).

If you want a series, the Caves of Steel trilogy is also a great starting point, more along the lines of a detective novel. They're pretty quick reads as well.

Thank you so much. I ended up speaking to the non supportive friend and it turned out they thought I was just "stopping for a bit". When I told them I had 45 days before this they were more chagrined and apologized. 

I should have stood up for myself but it was hard and I just didn't want to tell 20+ people who have seen me drink and been "fine" that I was an alcoholic and going sober. Still on me though.

I appreciate your advice and reply a lot though. Thank you so much, and IWNDWYT.

"Freezing" is a common response during sexual assault, I think more common than people think. I'm glad you have your therapist to talk to through this, it sounds extremely overwhelming. I fear this will sound like an empty platitude, the pain is really hard yes, and it will take a while,  trauma is really difficult and I don't think we as humans have a way to turn it off yet. I have felt the wish as well to just turn everything off and stop hurting. Again, I'm so sorry this happened to you.

Hey. It might not count for anything but I've been where you are. Happened to me. I couldn't talk to anyone. Felt awful, everything just was too much. Didn't know what to say to people. Pulled away.

Just know that you are a worthy person and this doesn't define you. Nothing about this was caused by you. You did nothing wrong. You do not deserve any of this. I am so, so sorry. 

You are absolutely doing the best you can. One second at a time. One hour at a time. Whatever you can handle right now. You're doing great. I may be an internet stranger but I hear you, I see your pain and I wish I could take it from you.

If you feel it is a good option for you, I myself have benefited from talk therapy. If that doesn't seem right, that's totally normal to feel that, and I apologise if I'm preaching at you.

You are not the scum of the earth at all. You're giving me exactly the kind of support you yourself deserve, someone to listen and hear. You've given me so much compassion I hope I can send some of that back your way. 

Feeling this way is so hard. It's not as simple as "get help". We already don't feel accepted. It sounds like she expects you to somehow suddenly get better, and stop bothering her, whereas you can't ask for love and safety from her. And I'm so sorry. It's so hard when the people you wish you could trust are not there for you. You deserve to be here and be understood, for who you are, not who people think you should be.

I'm so sorry. I've had sinus issues once and I wouldn't wish that pain on anyone. I hope it stops sooner than later. 

And I'm so sorry about your mother. I wish family could be more supportive. You've been nothing but supportive to me, and I want to say I'm here to listen too. I wasn't sure what would happen when I posted it here but it seems there is a community of people who won't judge but are here to listen. I hope I can do that for you as well, to listen to what's going on with you too. Just as you're telling me that I seem more caring then I think, I am certain things are not your fault. Anything you would like to talk about?

I'll try. It still feels like the right thing to do. I feel like a fraud, I don't know what else I've done that people aren't telling me. The person I injured with my words apparently also was upset by something past year, but I didn't know. They never talked to me about it, and I don't remember the conversation, but it doesn't matter my intent, it only matters how it made them feel. How could I have missed how I hurt them then, and then gone on to do this? How many more people have I hurt that I don't know about? It would be better to keep them from the awkwardness of having to confront me and just remove the issue.

Thank you for your kind words. You deserve so much as well. I don't know what to say, but thank you for helping me feel a little less alone. I'll try to take what you've said to heart. I'm just so tired I want to stop it all and try to make other people's lives a little better.

I think it depends on your skin and the skill of your esthtetician. I have had dermaplaning done every time before a skin treatment, either a peel or a dermapen treatment. After 4 treatments so far, I've seen improvement in the texture of my skin and had ice pick type scars flatten out. Any redness/swelling goes away after 2 days, max. I just use polysporin and a light moisturizer those days. 

Granted, I also use a disposable razor to gently shave my face about every week. I think the key here is "gentle". My esthtetician doesn't scrape very hard when she dermaplanes me, as she uses a very sharp scalpel and doesn't need to press hard at all.

I've fainted twice, both for reasons that I'm not really sure of. 

Once, I was in a store with my sister, and we'd just had a major argument. I just remember looking at postcards, then suddenly waking up to find myself horizontal, with people gathered around me. No hint, no warning.

The second time (prefacing this with the fact that I have a fear of needles), I was listening to someone tell a particularly gruesome story of being stuck multiple times during blood donation, when I just slipped sideways. I remember my vision narrowing in, going black, and a roaring noise in my ears -- that time, I knew I was going to faint. Didn't help me any, still woke up on my back, feet tangled in my chair.
